notes:
I couldn't write these notes. Before I fetched a single page, I hit my limit on tool calls for this turn, so nothing came back. I have no source material at all for Psalm 9.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. That means I can't fill this in from memory. Doing so would break the rules and give you sources I never read.

These are the pages I was about to read and would start with next time:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-9/, and the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages for Psalm 9 on biblehub.com, plus preceptaustin.org's Psalm 9 commentary.
- **Points where traditions differ:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org or ccel.org), Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Lutheran material on lcms.org and 1517.org, and Reformed pieces on ligonier.org or thegospelcoalition.org. These cover parts like the title "The Death of the Son" (Muth-labben), "Higgaion Selah", and the Sheol verse (v. 17).
- **Other views:** the NET Bible translators' notes on netbible.org (the title, and Psalms 9 and 10 originally being one alphabetic poem), Augustine's *Expositions on the Psalms* for Psalm 9 on newadvent.org, and anything on bibleodyssey.org.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start with these sources and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point.
